agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — TOOL_STEP hand-off was missing instructions_ref and controls
summary_for_principal: You asked what an agent gets handed when a step is an AI-judgment one; answering it surfaced a real, already-specified gap. The rulebook itself already says the hand-off should carry three things — the resolved inputs, a reference to the instructions to follow, and what the output will be checked against — but the engine only ever sent the first. An agent picking up a step had no way to know which skill it was meant to follow or what it would be graded on, short of going and looking the Tool up itself. Fixed to match what the rulebook already specified: both are now included in every step hand-off. Two new tests, plus the existing one extended. Full suite: 307 tests pass.

also.reason: One new test with a Tool declaring real, mixed-kind controls (profile + conventions) to prove both new fields carry real content, not just null defaults; one existing hand-off test extended with the same assertions.

S508 (S12.1) already states the exact shape this fix now matches: "TOOL_STEP (a non-deterministic step for the caller's agent session: resolved inputs, instructions ref, controls)" — confirmed this was a pure implementation gap against already-correct spec text, not something needing a spec change.

interpretation.read_as: Close the specific, already-identified, already-agreed gap from the immediately preceding exchange: the TOOL_STEP hand-off's missing instructions_ref/controls, as distinct from the separate, larger AGENTIC-redesign question raised in the same message, which was left open for further discussion rather than closed here.

filled_in.gap: The spec names "instructions ref" and "controls" but doesn't give a JSON/Python shape for either.
filled_in.assumed: `instructions_ref` is the Tool's own `mechanism.ref` (S4.3 already names this as "a skill document" for SKILL, "a skill or agent definition" for AGENTIC — exactly what an instructions reference is), and `controls` is a plain tuple of `{kind, ref}` mappings mirroring the Tool's own declared `ControlRef`s verbatim, rather than resolving each control's full definition (title, checker, threshold) into the answer — the caller already has the same Process/Registry and can look up a control's own definition by its `kind`/`ref` if it needs more than the reference.
filled_in.grounded_in: S4.3's own table naming exactly what a mechanism's `ref` points to per kind; "hold conventions once" — the caller is already assumed (by resolved_inputs' own existing design) to hold the same Process/Registry, so duplicating full control definitions into every answer would be redundant with what the caller can already resolve itself.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Cheap — additive fields with `None`/empty defaults; every existing NextAnswer construction site left unchanged continues to produce the same values it always did for these two new fields (None and empty-tuple-only-where-populated).

decisions.headline: instructions_ref carries the Tool's mechanism.ref verbatim; controls carries the Tool's own declared ControlRefs as plain {kind, ref} mappings, not their resolved definitions.
decisions.problem: S508 says the TOOL_STEP answer should carry "instructions ref" and "controls" but does not specify a wire shape for either — the engine needed to pick one.
options_rejected: Resolve each control's full Control document (or Profile schema, for a profile: control) into the answer, rather than just its kind/ref: rejected — the caller already holds the same Registry that resolved_inputs' own design already assumes, so this would duplicate information the caller can already look up itself, and would need to decide (schema? every field?) how much of a Control's own definition to inline, none of which S508's own text asks for.

Name the new field `instructions` (the actual resolved skill document content) rather than `instructions_ref`: rejected — S508's own words are "instructions ref", and resolving a skill document's actual prose content is a different, larger question (where do skill documents live, how are they loaded) that this fix does not need to answer to close the gap as stated.
decisions.cost_to_change: Additive dataclass fields; a future change to carry richer control/instruction content would only need to add fields, not remove these.

evidence.claim: Before this fix, `NextAnswer` for a `TOOL_STEP` carried only `resolved_inputs` — confirmed by reading the one construction site directly before making any change.

evidence.claim: Both fields now carry real content end to end: a Tool with a SKILL mechanism and two controls of different kinds (profile, conventions) produces a hand-off with the exact mechanism ref and both controls, in order.
